- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (all 0.00) and price history shows low volatility, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; if true outcome deviates >5% from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted downward 1–2 days before sentiment turns negative.
